entries.name: Diagonal structured state space model
entries.definition: A diagonal state-space sequence-model family that computes its discretized convolution kernel by a Vandermonde product, with explicit choices of discretization, state-matrix constraint and initialization.
entries.identity_notes: S4D is the family defined by Gu and colleagues, distinguished from S4's diagonal-plus-low-rank construction. The paper separates the earlier DSS configuration and the S4D-LegS, S4D-Inv and S4D-Lin initialization choices rather than treating all diagonal models as identical.
entries.mechanism: Discretize a diagonal continuous-time state model using bilinear or zero-order-hold rules. Kernel entries are sums of output and input coefficients multiplied by powers of the discretized diagonal state entries. Constrain the continuous state eigenvalue real parts using the chosen parameterization and initialize their spectrum according to the selected variant.
entries.locator: Sections 3.1–3.4 and 4, equations 6–9 and Table 1, PDF/printed pp. 4–6
limitations: Algebraic diagonalizability does not guarantee numerically stable representation or successful optimization; initialization and discretization remain explicit choices.
S4D-LegS convergence to the corresponding S4 dynamics is an infinite-state-size statement, not exact equality of all finite S4D and S4 models.
The inverse-law spectral asymptotics are presented as Conjecture 4, not a proved theorem. No universal performance advantage is asserted.

entries.mapping_rationale: This is a parameterized family of linear sequence models; Model is broader and does not conflate the core with the nonlinear architectures built from it.
entries.abstract_interpretation: Studies diagonal state-space parameterizations, initialization and their relationship to S4/DSS. The record distinguishes algebraic expressivity, finite-dimensional approximation and training behavior; abstract performance claims are not generalized.

entries.name: High-order polynomial projection operators
entries.definition: A family of time-dependent operators that represents a signal's past by coefficients of its optimal finite-dimensional polynomial approximation under a chosen time-varying measure.
entries.identity_notes: HiPPO denotes the general projection-and-coefficient framework, not one fixed state matrix, a complete recurrent neural network, or only the scaled-Legendre instantiation HiPPO-LegS. The qualified acronym distinguishes this operator family from the unrelated highlight-replay PPO method.
entries.mechanism: At each time, project the available signal history onto a polynomial subspace by minimizing the measure-weighted squared approximation error, then extract coefficients in the associated orthogonal basis. For the derived measure families, differentiating those coefficients yields linear differential dynamics that can be discretized as online recurrences.
entries.locator: Sections 2.1–2.4, Definition 1 and Figure 1, PDF/printed pp. 2–5
limitations: Optimality is relative to the chosen measure and finite polynomial subspace, not lossless recovery of arbitrary history or optimal downstream prediction.

A tractable closed-form recurrence is not asserted for every arbitrary measure. The translated-Legendre sliding-window update additionally approximates the unavailable boundary value; numerical discretization adds its own approximation.
entries.title: HiPPO: Recurrent Memory with Optimal Polynomial Projections
entries.mapping_rationale: Definition 1 and the coefficient/projection composition define operators mapping an input function to coefficient values through time. MathematicalFunction is broader than this specific family of mathematical rules; no complete neural-network identity is asserted.
entries.abstract_interpretation: Introduces a polynomial-projection framework for online signal-history compression and a scaled-Legendre instantiation. Optimality concerns a specified approximation problem, not lossless memory or guaranteed prediction quality.

entries.name: Scaled Legendre HiPPO operator
entries.definition: The HiPPO projection operator using the uniform measure over the full elapsed interval from zero to the current time, with scaled-Legendre coefficients evolving under explicitly time-dependent linear memory dynamics.
entries.identity_notes: HiPPO-LegS is the scaled-Legendre instantiation of the broader HiPPO framework. Its time-dependent operator differs from a fixed state matrix used to initialize a later S4 model and from the fixed-width translated-Legendre window.
entries.mechanism: Use the normalized uniform measure on [0,t] and the corresponding Legendre basis. For positive time, the coefficient derivative is minus A times the current coefficient vector divided by t, plus B times the current signal divided by t; the source specifies a lower-triangular A and a fixed B and derives discrete recurrences from these dynamics.
entries.locator: Section 3, Theorem 2, equations 3–4 and footnote 3, with Sections 2.1–2.4 for projection context; PDF/printed pp. 3–5
limitations: The displayed differential formula contains 1/t and applies for positive t; an executable initialization at the time origin is not supplied by this record.

Equation 4 illustrates an Euler discretization; the paper also uses bilinear and zero-order-hold schemes. The operator's approximation properties do not guarantee arbitrary downstream-network accuracy.
entries.title: HiPPO: Recurrent Memory with Optimal Polynomial Projections

entries.abstract_interpretation: Introduces a polynomial-projection framework for online signal-history compression and a scaled-Legendre instantiation. Optimality concerns a specified approximation problem, not lossless memory or guaranteed prediction quality.

entries.name: Linear state-space layer
entries.definition: A sequence-to-sequence layer defined by discretizing a linear continuous-time state-space system, with a state recurrence and, for zero initial state, an equivalent convolutional representation plus a direct input term.
entries.identity_notes: LSSL denotes Gu and colleagues' component with state-space parameters and timescale, not the complete deep LSSL network, every recurrent network, or S4's later structured parameterization and kernel algorithm.
entries.mechanism: Discretize the state dynamics using a step size to obtain a recurrent state update and linear output map. With zero initial state, powers of the discretized state matrix between input and output projections form the convolution kernel. Separate feature channels use their own broadcast input/output parameters and timescales; complete networks add further layers and connections.
entries.locator: Section 2 equations 3–5 and Sections 3.1–3.3, equations 6–7, PDF/printed pp. 4–6
limitations: The simple convolution expression assumes zero initial state; a nonzero starting state contributes an additional term.

The layer is linear; nonlinear expressive power of stacked networks is not a property of a single standalone LSSL. Efficient recurrent updates and kernel construction depend on the selected state-matrix structure.
entries.title: Combining Recurrent, Convolutional, and Continuous-time Models with Linear State-Space Layers

entries.abstract_interpretation: Introduces a sequence layer connecting continuous state dynamics, recurrent evaluation and convolutional computation. Deep networks built from such layers are separate from the linear component.

entries.name: FlashConv
entries.definition: An execution algorithm for state-space sequence convolutions that fuses FFT-based convolution in GPU on-chip memory, uses block FFT matrix multiplications and passes state between chunks for longer sequences.
entries.identity_notes: FlashConv is the convolution-execution contribution in the H3 paper, distinct from the H3 layer and from FlashAttention's attention-computation algorithm.
entries.mechanism: Fuse the FFT, pointwise spectral product and inverse FFT to avoid intermediate off-chip transfers; factor the FFT into block matrix multiplications suited to specialized hardware. When the sequence exceeds the chosen on-chip working capacity, compute chunk convolutions and propagate the state-space boundary state between chunks.
limitations: The paper's 8K on-chip threshold concerns its stated A100 setting; no device-independent cutoff or wall-clock speedup is asserted.
Block FFT may use more arithmetic than a conventional FFT while exploiting specialized matrix hardware.

The printed Algorithm 2 mixes chunk variable names and its exact boundary indexing was not implemented or verified here. This record supports the execution strategy, not a certified literal transcription of the pseudocode.
entries.title: Hungry Hungry Hippos: Towards Language Modeling with State Space Models
entries.mapping_rationale: FlashConv computes one-dimensional sequence convolutions, an operation used by this AIO layer. The algorithm concerns execution and state passing rather than denoting the layer itself, so the mapping is related rather than broader-class membership.
entries.abstract_interpretation: The H3 abstract introduces a separate hardware-execution contribution alongside the H3 layer. Sections 4.1–4.2 support the fused convolution and chunk state-passing strategy, without establishing a universal hardware speedup.
